coach_says: Taking back with the queen leaves your e6 pawn blocking your c8 bishop, so White plays Qg4 and hits g7. You can't defend it comfortably and have to play Kf8, giving up castling for good. Recapturing with the pawn (exd5) opens the c8 bishop's diagonal to g4, so Qg4 is impossible and your king can still castle. Before recapturing with the queen in the opening, check what the opponent's queen can attack next.
also: king loses the right to castle

coach_says: On b3 your queen stands right in front of Black's queenside pawns, and ...c4 kicks it away while also hitting d3. You lose time retreating to c2, Black opens lines with ...cxd3, and then ...Bd6 hits your knight on h2 while your king is still on e1. Castle first (O-O) and keep the queen where pawns can't chase it.
also: castle before bringing the queen out

coach_says: Attacking the queen with ...Bg4 only sends it to b3, a better square, where it lines up with Bc4 on f7 and g8 and also eyes b7. Now Bf7+ followed by Bxg6 is a threat because nothing defends g6, and after f3 your bishop has no good retreat. Develop a piece that helps instead, like ...Nc6, which hits d4. Before chasing a queen, ask where it will go and what it does there.
concept: chasing the queen to a better square

coach_says: Your a4 pawn was attacked by the bishop on d7 and nothing defended it, and Ng4 doesn't change that, so Black just takes it with ...Bxa4. Black wins a pawn and gets a passed a-pawn heading towards your king on c1. Ask what your opponent's last move threatens before you start your own plan: b3 would have kept the pawn and held the queenside together.
